content:
ana: Heads-up — I'm starting the AWS KMS integration for Redwood Private (customer VPC BYOK). Two parallel concerns: control-plane CMK for metadata/DEK wrapping, and data-plane DEKs used by inference nodes. Need guidance on cross-account grants, a safe rewrap/rotation workflow, RBAC tweaks, and the minimum CloudTrail/KMS events to watch. @sam @morgan any quick hits?

sam: Short version: customer supplies CMK (BYOK) in their account for control-plane. We do envelope encryption: platform generates per-customer DEKs, encrypts DEKs with the customer CMK, stores ciphertext in our control-plane DB. Runtime instances get short-lived decrypt grants. Use KMS grants (not long-term IAM kms:Decrypt).

morgan: Agree. Important details: 1) Use encryption-context with keys {"customer_id","purpose":"dek"} and require EncryptionContextEquals in the key policy, 2) Create grants with operations ["Decrypt","ReEncryptFrom","ReEncryptTo"] and set the grantTokens/retire flow, 3) Never bake kms:Decrypt in instance role policies. Example grant creation (CLI):

```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/customer-cmk --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-runtime --operations Decrypt ReEncryptFrom ReEncryptTo --name "runtime-decrypt-<customer>"
```

And store the returned GrantId so we can revoke/retire it if needed.

jess: Rotation note: when the customer rotates CMK (or we need to rotate for compromise), we must rewrap their DEKs. Plan: batch rewrap worker that reads DB, for each encrypted DEK call ReEncrypt specifying DestinationKeyId=new-key and supply same encryption-context. Track progress per-customer and use checkpoints; test on a canary customer first. If anything fails, snapshot ciphertexts before modifying so we can rollback. Also ensure CloudTrail records KMS ReEncrypt events — that should be an alerting signal.

infra-sre: Minimal runtime IAM policy snippet (granting only STS assume + KMS via grants):

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":"sts:AssumeRole","Resource":"arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-runtime"},
    {"Effect":"Deny","Action":"kms:Decrypt","Resource":"*"}  // explicit deny so only grants work
  ]
}
```

We enforce decrypt via grants. Also rotate grant TTLs by expiring them every X hours and renewing on first request.

sec-bot: Runbook link added: /internal/runbooks/kms-private-vpc-dek-rewrap. Includes compromise playbook: disable CMK, disable grants, switch to fallback key, and contact customer.

ana: (typo -> ana) Q: how do we revoke grants fast if we suspect key compromise?

sam: Two quick flows: 1) RevokeGrant for each GrantId (we should persist GrantIds for all active grants), 2) Disable the CMK (customer action) which blocks operations immediately. For cross-account grants the grantee is the runtime role in our account — the customer can retire grants or call RevokeGrant. If a revoke is slow, rotate to a new CMK and switch to it as fallback; run rewrap as background job.

morgan: On audit/monitoring: ensure CloudTrail + CloudWatch log group for KMS events with these actions: kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:ReEncrypt, kms:CreateGrant, kms:RetireGrant, kms:RevokeGrant. Add metric filters for spikes in ReEncrypt or RevokeGrant (could indicate mass rewrap or attack). Also log EncryptionContext values where possible (CloudTrail shows them).

jess: RBAC change idea: create a short-lived key-admin role that can be assumed only with MFA and approval (PagerDuty workflow). Only keys admins can request customer rewraps. Developers do not get direct KMS perms.

deploy-bot: rotation-job@staging completed for canary-customer (0 errors).

ana: Next steps/action items: 1) @morgan to draft exact IAM/grant policy examples and sample CLI flows, 2) @jess to add rewrap runbook sections (checkpointing, snapshot rollback, canary plan), 3) @sam to prototype grant lifecycle code (create, store GrantId, revoke/retire). I'll coordinate BYOK onboarding with the customer infra lead. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll add a small CLI snippet for rewrap (example):

```bash
# re-encrypt a stored ciphertext blob using new key
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc_dek.blob --destination-key-id alias/new-cmk --source-encryption-context \"{\"customer_id\":\"cust-123\",\"purpose\":\"dek\"}\" --destination-encryption-context \"{\"customer_id\":\"cust-123\",\"purpose\":\"dek\"}\" --output text > rewrapped.blob
```

morgan: One more operational note — use grant tokens carefully. They are transient and can help in bootstrap flows but don't rely on them for long-lived auth. Persist GrantIds if you need to revoke. Also consider tagging grants with "redwood:customer=cust-123" for traceability.

ana: Great — thanks team. I'll open a PR linking the draft policies and runbook sections once we have initial text.
